name: Hottentot

pitch_detail.notes: Moves right and up a slab; reported as not freed as of 2015.

descent_text: Lower/rappel from the P1 chains is documented; the descent from the P2 slab is unknown — verify current beta before attempting the full route.
approach: Summertime Crag uses a different trailhead than the other four areas' shared Blue Lake approach. From Winthrop, drive west on SR-20 through Mazama toward Washington Pass (or, coming from Seattle, continue past Washington Pass toward Mazama on SR-20); park at a small pullout on the east side of the highway, just before the larger 'Spires Gully' parking area used to access the Early Winters Spires from the east. From the pullout, descend off the road down through trees, cross Early Winters Creek, follow it briefly downstream, then climb up-slope and contour left to reach the crag — about a 20-25 minute walk with minimal elevation change. The crag stays shaded until mid-afternoon in summer, making it a popular warm-weather alternative when Mazama-area cragging runs hot.
overview: The crag's hardest-rated line, starting from the rightmost position: a bolted 5.10+ first pitch to chains, then a right-trending second pitch onto a slab whose grade and free-climbing status were unconfirmed as of the last documented ascent (2015).
beta: P1 climbs past bolts to chains at roughly 5.10+. P2 moves right and up a slab reported as possibly 5.12 and not freed as of 2015, so the pitch's grade and completion status are unresolved.
gear: Quickdraws — Hottentot is a bolt-protected sport line at Summertime Crag, not a trad route
60-70m rope; several routes at this crag are long enough to want the extra length
Helmet — common practice at this crag even though it's fully bolted
